chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Musa ibn al-Hasan, from Abu al-Hasan al-Nahdi who raised the chain of narration, said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) used to say: 'Whoever dies before (the age of) forty, then (his life) has been cut short; and whoever dies within less than fourteen days (of illness), then his death is a sudden death.'

key_terms.اخْتُرِمَ: Ikhtirām — the verb means to be snatched away prematurely; a life cut short before its full span
key_terms.رَفَعَ الْحَدِيثَ: Rafa'a al-hadith — a technical hadith term meaning the narrator elevated/attributed the narration to the Prophet or Imam without naming all intermediate links (mursal)
key_terms.مَوْتُ فَجْأَةٍ: Sudden death (mawt faj'a) — dying without prolonged illness or warning; distinct from expected natural death

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of sudden death (mawt faj'a) in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (peace be upon him) provides two jurisprudential definitions related to sudden death (mawt faj'a). First, dying before the age of forty is considered a premature or abrupt end to one's life (ikhtirām). Second, dying within fewer than fourteen days of falling ill constitutes sudden death. This hadith is transmitted through a mursal chain, meaning al-Nahdi omitted intermediate narrators between himself and the Imam, indicating the hadith's reliance on earlier, unnamed transmitters. These definitions carry significance in Islamic law (fiqh) regarding wills, inheritance, and ritual preparations.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Musa Bin Al Hassan, from Abu Al Hassan Al Nahdy, raising the Hadeeth, said,
‘Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘The one who dies below (the age of) forty, so (his life is) cut (short); and the one who dies in less than fourteen days (of illness), so his death is sudden’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Musa ibn al-Hassan from abu al-Hassan al-Nahdi in a mafu’ manner who has said the following: “

Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘If one dies before the age of forty, his life is cut short, and if one dies before fourteen days from the day of his falling ill, such death is a sudden death.’”
